text: Three departments request different features for a volunteer scheduling product. In Scrum, who is accountable for ordering these requests in the Product Backlog?

options.text: The Product Owner, considering value, the Product Goal and stakeholder input.
Whichever department sends the most messages.
Each department independently, without a shared order.
The Scrum Master must personally choose the product priorities.

text: Mid-Sprint, Developers discover that a planned integration needs a different implementation. The Sprint Goal remains useful. What is an appropriate response?

options.text: Reduce the quality standard so the original task list looks complete.
Refuse any discussion because nothing may be learned during a Sprint.
Replace the Sprint Goal with an unrelated urgent request.
Discuss and renegotiate scope with the Product Owner while protecting the Sprint Goal and quality.

text: At a Daily Scrum, Developers notice that a blocked dependency threatens the Sprint Goal. What should the event help them do?

options.text: Wait for the Scrum Master to assign every remaining task.
Inspect the goal’s progress and adapt their upcoming plan together.
Read yesterday’s task counts to a manager and keep the plan unchanged.
Reorder the entire Product Backlog without the Product Owner.
